content: Hot off my PR the other day which renamed Pi.prod to Function.prod (#38963), this PR renames Pi.map to Function.map, so that in the future (i.e. when we have better dot-notation support for Function) we will be able to use dot notation here with ease.
#39233
I'd be hesitant to rename only this one; I think we should first answer the bigger question of "should we move everything out of the Pi namespace and into the Function namespace"?
(eg docs#Pi.add_def)
If the sole motivation is dot notation, then there is an alternative option of asking core to implement special support for Pi to match what already exists for Function.

I think that is a good point (and I would support it). Here is a counterpoint: this at least means Logic/Function/Defs contains no Pi. content (which to me makes sense as a desirable thing in and of itself).
Renaming docs#Pi.single to Function.single would also make a bunch of statements / goal states longer to read, though I guess a single open makes that problem go away

I think there's that and also it being somewhat inconsistent when Pi. and Function. are used - e.g. consider why is docs#Function.swap not instead Pi.flip (and indeed why is docs#flip not docs#Function.flip, but this is a core issue).

I think also given that pi notation is no longer used in Lean (as I believe it was when these things were first named) there is a real case for making the change. I am sympathetic to the argument that it is worth differentiating between dependent and non-dependent cases - but we just changed Pi.prod to Function.prod, so we clearly don't always believe that.

Wrenna Robson said:

I think also given that pi notation is no longer used in Lean

It is used in mathlib still,

import Mathlib
#check Π i, Fin i

If it's a question of length, incidentally, I think Fun would be a better name than Pi nowadays (because of the fun => notation), except that clearly having a Fun. and Function. namespace could be confusing.
That is true! But relatively a lot less than it once was in terms of actual usage.
Can you edit the first post to link the Pi.prod PR?
Now I look at, say, docs#Pi.algebra and to me this is a great example of where it does make sense, because on some level this is indeed a product (what is suggested by Pi).
Pi.map is arguably mapping a function over a product

Eric Wieser said:

Can you edit the first post to link the Pi.prod PR?

Done

Eric Wieser said:

Pi.map is arguably mapping a function over a product

Yeah, I am not unsympathetic to this. Equally I might note that it is kinda "just" dependent composition if you squint (dependent composition is quite an odd operation to use in practice but that is a different discussion).
The signature of Pi.map is (approximately) (∀ i, α i → β i) → (∀ i, α i) → (∀ i, β i). Which of these two arguments is used by (or should be used by) dot notation?

If you think it's the (∀ i, α i), well, we would I think need special support for that to work in this order with dot notation, but it is not unreasonable on some level. It's consistent with Prod.map. Equally one might feel that you want a fixed (f : ∀ i, α i → β i) and f.map a should mean "apply the product of maps that f represents to the product a".
I think in general we want map f : (∀ i, α i) → (∀ i, β i), but that forces dot notation to do the wrong thing compared to List.map f.
Yes, there is no way I think to say "hey, this is the argument we want to dot".
List.mapFinIdx is probably the slightly better analogy actually.
In that that is like, I have a list, I apply a map to each element of the list, that map is dependent on the index.

The dot notation here is consistent with Prod.map. So I do actually see what you're saying - that we want the second argument in (∀ i, α i → β i) → (∀ i, α i) → (∀ i, β i) to be the dot notation variable, but we DO want it to be the second argument, and we don't really have a way of signifying that.
I didn't intend to present #39233 as a fait accompli to be clear - I am glad we're having this discussion.
Another name candidate would be Function.pi to match docs#LinearMap.pi edit: docs#LinearMap.piMap is indeed the correct comparison
Right I was just about to say, name it like docs#LinearMap.pi.
Ah we got to the same place :)
Yeah I think Function.pi and Pi.map, on reflection, might be the two names you want. But then there is also docs#LinearMap.piMap
Honestly, that is quite weird because in many other places piMap is used it seems to be asserting a predicate about Pi.map.
Honestly though LinearMap.pi has a fixed domain and dependent codomain, it isn't as much like Pi.map.
(Consider also Equiv.piComm versus Function.swap!)
I think this then raises that LinearMap.piMap ought to be renamed alongside your change to LinearMap.functionMap or similar; the old name was indictaing "this is the linear version of Pi.map"
Yeah I considered it but didn't want to be overzealous.
I think you should at least declare what the end goal looks like in the PR description, even if you don't intend to get there in one step
(or perhaps in #mathlib4, then link the zulip thread)
Ah, what do you mean exactly?
#mathlib4 > The Pi namespace
I think I figured it out
So nobody replied to this post. I would prefer that this PR not be delayed further - or rather I do not know what action I could possibly take to advance it.
